title: Handles Under Fatigue
description: Players sprint a full court, then immediately perform a precise ball-handling sequence, training control when the legs and lungs are tired.

content.objective: Keep dribble quality, footwork and decisions when fatigued, as in the last minutes of a game.
content.setup: A ball rests on a cone at half court; players start on the baseline.
content.organization: Waves of two to four; work 40 seconds, rest 40 seconds.
instructions: Sprint to the far baseline and back to half court.
Pick up the ball and perform 10 crossovers, 10 between-the-legs and 10 behind-the-back, stationary and low.
Speed-dribble to the near rim and finish.
Rest while the next wave goes.
coachingPoints: Quality before speed in the stationary block, even when tired.
Breathe out on the moves; stay low.
Finish strong: tired players miss lay-ups by slowing down.
commonMistakes: Sloppy, high dribbles because of fatigue.
content.safety: Build up sets over weeks; stop anyone showing dizziness. Water available between sets.
progressions: Add a defender who pressures the final speed dribble.
regressions: Reduce each move to five reps.
variations: Replace the moves with a two-ball block.
Finish with a free throw instead of a lay-up.
successCriteria: Completes the handling block with no lost ball after the sprint.
Makes the finish on at least 4 of 5 sets.
content.gameApplication: Turnovers rise late in games; ball handlers who practise tired protect the ball when it matters.
content.repetitions: 4 to 6 sets, 40 s work / 40 s rest
